Prerequisite: A FortiNAC license key at the Base level or higher, with enough concurrent licenses for the hosts and devices online, that includes the licensed features in use (Device Profiler, Guest Manager, Endpoint Compliance, Integration Suite)
What it enables: Network discovery, host profiling, and classification, and the licensed features the key includes; when the concurrent license count is exceeded, no new registrations are allowed and network access provisioning based on policy does not occur
How to put it in place: Install the key from Fortinet (on a VM, during the configuration wizard); GUI: System > Settings > System management > License management (Modify License Key; check License Name, Concurrent Licenses, and the feature fields)
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Licenses" (license types, license count, concurrent licenses) and "License management" (Settings); FortiNAC F 7.2.0 Administration Guide, "Licenses" (Base: network discovery, host profiling, and classification)

Prerequisite: A FortiNAC license key at the Plus level or higher
What it enables: Host registration, scanning, and access control (the Plus features, which include all Base features)
How to put it in place: Buy and install a Plus or Pro key; GUI: System > Settings > System management > License management (License Name: Plus or Pro)
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Licenses" (license types) and "License management" (License Name: Base, Plus, or Pro); FortiNAC F 7.2.0 Administration Guide, "Licenses"

Prerequisite: A FortiNAC license key at the Pro level, with Security Incidents licenses
What it enables: Automated Threat Response (Security Incidents): security rules, triggers, and actions on events from security devices; without the Security Incidents license its features cannot be accessed
How to put it in place: Buy and install a Pro key; GUI: System > Settings > System management > License management (License Name: Pro; Security Incidents Licenses)
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Licenses" (Pro: Automated Threat Response), "License management" (Security Incidents Licenses), and "Security Incidents"

Prerequisite: The isolation interface (port2) with the isolation scopes and the DHCP, DNS, and HTTPS services that the isolation networks and the captive portal use
What it enables: Registration, remediation, and dead-end isolation networks, where FortiNAC serves IP addresses and DNS to isolated hosts, and the captive portal
How to put it in place: Define the isolation interface and scopes with GUI: System > Config wizard; config system global; set portal port2; end; config system interface; edit port2; append allowaccess dhcp dns https; next; end
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Config wizard" (isolation interface port2) and "Open ports" ("FortiNAC Access Configuration": isolation scopes and captive portal need dhcp, dns, and https on port2); FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 CLI Reference Guide, interface context (allowaccess)

Prerequisite: The network devices that FortiNAC manages (switches, wireless controllers and access points, firewalls, VPN devices) modeled in Inventory with an IPv4 address and working SNMP and CLI credentials, and SNMP allowed on port1
What it enables: Discovery, polling, and host location, and enforcement on the device (VLAN switching, ACLs, CoA); L3 (IP to MAC) polling is supported only on Cisco, Juniper EX, HP ProCurve, Brocade, and FortiGate devices
How to put it in place: GUI: Network > Inventory (Add Device with SNMPv3 credentials; Credentials tab, Validate Credentials); config system interface; edit port1; append allowaccess snmp; next; end
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Add or modify a device" (SNMP device, snmp in set allowaccess), "Credentials", "Model configuration" (CLI user name), and "IPv6 support" (device management needs IPv4; L3 polling vendors)

Prerequisite: The access value of each logical network on each modeled device (VLAN ID or name, ACL, filter ID, role, VPN group policy, or CoA profile)
What it enables: Enforcement of network access policies, registration and remediation networks, and quarantine on the device
How to put it in place: GUI: Network > Inventory > Device configuration > Model configuration (logical network access values for the device)
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Model configuration" and "Network access" (Policy & Objects; Access Value: VLAN ID, VLAN name, Aruba role, or VPN group policy)

Prerequisite: User/host profiles that select the users and hosts a policy applies to
What it enables: Authentication policies and endpoint compliance policies, which map a profile to a configuration
How to put it in place: GUI: Policy & Objects > User/host profiles
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "User/host profiles", "Authentication" (Policy & Objects), and "Endpoint compliance" ("Policies")

Prerequisite: A FortiNAC agent on the endpoints (the Persistent Agent installed, or the Dissolvable Agent from the captive portal), the current agent package on FortiNAC, and agent communication allowed on the interface
What it enables: Posture scans, status notifications, and remediation of endpoints (the Persistent Agent uses TCP 4568, and TCP 80 for upgrades; the Dissolvable Agent requires a valid third-party SSL certificate, not a self-signed one)
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Settings > Updates > Agent packages; install the agent on the hosts (MSI, GPO, or the portal); config system interface; edit <PORT>; append allowaccess nac-agent http; next; end
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Persistent Agent" (communication; setup requirements: nac-agent and http in set allowaccess), "Dissolvable Agent" (setup requirements), and "Agent packages"

Prerequisite: A DoD-issued server certificate for each certificate target in use (Admin UI, Portal, Persistent Agent, Local RADIUS Server for EAP, RadSec, SAML)
What it enables: TLS for the Admin UI, the portal, and the agents, EAP termination (the local RADIUS server requires a server certificate), RadSec, and SAML
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Certificate management (Generate CSR for the target, submit it to the DoD CA, Upload the certificate)
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Certificates" (uses and requirements), "Obtain a certificate from CA" (targets), and "Configure Local RADIUS Server settings" (requires a server certificate for EAP)

Prerequisite: The DoD root and intermediate CA certificates in each trusted certificate target in use (RADIUS Endpoint Trust for EAP-TLS and RadSec, SAML Trust, General Trusted CA)
What it enables: Validation of client certificates for EAP-TLS, PEAP-EAP-TLS, EAP-TTLS/EAP-TLS, TEAP, and RadSec (a client cannot authenticate unless its root certificate is installed), of SAML identity providers, and of devices over SSL
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Certificate management > Trusted certificates (select the target; add the DoD root and intermediate certificates)
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Trusted certificates" (targets; RADIUS Endpoint Trust [radius]) and "Configure Local RADIUS Server settings" (Client Certificate Required)

Prerequisite: An OCSP responder for the DoD CA that FortiNAC can reach
What it enables: Real-time revocation checking of client certificates by the local RADIUS server
How to put it in place: Make the DoD-approved OCSP responder reachable from FortiNAC and allow for its response time in the OCSP Timeout
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Configure Local Server" (OCSP Enabled, Timeout, OCSP Soft Fail)

Prerequisite: An LDAP directory (such as Active Directory) with an account for FortiNAC, TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 enabled for SSL or TLS connections, and DNS resolution of its name
What it enables: Directory authentication of administrators and users, and synchronization of users, groups, and computer groups
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Settings > Authentication > Directories (connection, data field mapping, search branches, synchronization schedule)
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Directories" ("Requirements") and "Administrators" (Auth Type: LDAP)

Prerequisite: An external RADIUS server, with a validation account, defined as a RADIUS authentication source
What it enables: RADIUS authentication of administrators and of user registrations
How to put it in place: GUI: Network > Service Connectors > Authentication sources > RADIUS (server, RADIUS secret, ports, validation account)
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "RADIUS" (Authentication sources) and "Administrators" (Auth Type: RADIUS)

Prerequisite: A Microsoft Entra ID tenant with an application registered for FortiNAC
What it enables: Entra ID as an authentication source for 802.1X and portal login, and Entra ID group mapping (7.6.3 and later)
How to put it in place: Register the application as the Microsoft Entra ID Authentication Guide describes and select it in GUI: Network > RADIUS > Configure Local Server (Authentication Source)
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.3 Release Notes, "What's new" (Entra ID as native authentication source); FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Configure Local Server" (Authentication Source)

Prerequisite: A SAML 2.0 identity provider for administrators or portal users (7.6.3 and later)
What it enables: Admin SAML SSO and User SAML SSO, with role mapping from the identity provider
How to put it in place: Configure the identity provider and the SAML target and SAML Trust certificates; GUI: Network > Service Connectors > Admin SAML SSO
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.3 Release Notes, "What's new" (SAML SSO enhancements); FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Admin SAML SSO", "User SAML SSO", "Obtain a certificate from CA" (SAML target), and "Trusted certificates" (SAML Trust)

Prerequisite: An email server (SMTP) and, for SMS, an SMTP or REST SMS gateway
What it enables: Email and SMS notification of alarms, and delivery of administrator multi-factor authentication tokens
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Settings > System communication > Email settings (server, sender, authentication, Connection Security SSL/TLS or STARTTLS); GUI: Network > Service Connectors > Email/SMS > SMTP SMS Gateway
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Email settings", "Email/SMS" (SMTP and REST SMS gateways), and "Multi-factor Authentication" (token by email or SMS)

Prerequisite: External log receivers: a syslog server, FortiAnalyzer, SIEM, or SNMP trap receiver that FortiNAC can reach
What it enables: Off-loading of events and alarms (Syslog CSV, Syslog CEF, SNMP trap, FortiAnalyzer)
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Settings > System communication > Log receivers (Add; type, IP address, port)
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Log receivers" and "Log events to an external log host"; "Open ports" (syslog, UDP 514)

Prerequisite: NTP servers that FortiNAC can reach (UDP 123)
What it enables: Clock synchronization of each FortiNAC server
How to put it in place: Set during the configuration wizard; GUI: System > Settings > System management > NTP and time zone
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Config wizard" (NTP and time zone), "NTP and time zone", and "Open ports" (NTP, UDP 123)

Prerequisite: An SNMP manager that queries FortiNAC, using SNMPv3, and SNMP allowed on port1
What it enables: SNMP queries of FortiNAC and SNMPv3 traps that register hosts and users (the SNMP version is global, so every querying device must use it)
How to put it in place: config system interface; edit port1; append allowaccess snmp; next; end; configure the manager with the same SNMPv3 settings
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "SNMP" (System communication; snmp in set allowaccess)

Prerequisite: A remote backup server reachable over SSH or SFTP, with an account with write access and an existing remote path
What it enables: Copies of the database and system backups off the appliance
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Settings > System management > Remote backup configuration (server, user name, password, remote path)
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Remote backup configuration"

Prerequisite: Outbound access from port1 to the Fortinet update and FortiGuard servers
What it enables: Firmware upgrades from the download server, agent packages, auto-definition updates, license entitlements, and FortiGuard device lookups
How to put it in place: Allow port1 to reach fnac-updates.fortinet.net, fds1.fortinet.com, globalupdate.fortinet.net, and the FortiGuard device query servers listed in Open ports
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "FortiNAC CA Firewall Policy Requirements" (product updates, license entitlements, FortiGuard), "System" (Updates), "Agent packages", and "Auto-definition updates"

Prerequisite: The third-party or Fortinet platform behind a service connector (MDM, FortiClient EMS, OT platform, vulnerability scanner, CMDB, or ITSM), with an API account for FortiNAC
What it enables: Host data, compliance data, and device data from the platform, and incidents sent to it
How to put it in place: Create the API account on the platform; GUI: Network > Service Connectors (Create New; the connector for the platform)
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Service Connectors", "MDM Servers", "OT", "Vulnerability Scanners", and "ServiceNow ITSM Integration"

Prerequisite: The authenticators (switches, wireless controllers, VPN devices) configured to send RADIUS to FortiNAC, and the RADIUS services allowed on port1
What it enables: 802.1X and MAB through the local RADIUS server or a proxy virtual server, and CoA to the devices
How to put it in place: Configure each device with FortiNAC as its RADIUS server and the device's secret; config system interface; edit port1; append allowaccess radius-auth radius-acct; next; end
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Open ports" ("FortiNAC Access Configuration": radius-auth and radius-acct on port1) and "Configure Local RADIUS Server settings"

Prerequisite: 802.1X supplicants on the endpoints, with user or computer certificates issued by the DoD PKI for certificate-based EAP
What it enables: EAP-TLS, PEAP-EAP-TLS, EAP-TTLS/EAP-TLS, and TEAP authentication of users and machines
How to put it in place: Configure the supplicants and enroll the endpoints for DoD certificates
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Trusted certificates" (RADIUS Endpoint Trust [radius]: user or computer certificates), "Certificates" (supplicant configuration), and "Configure Local Server" (Client Certificate Attribute)

Prerequisite: Network and security devices configured to send syslog messages or SNMP traps to FortiNAC, and syslog allowed on port1
What it enables: MAC notification and link events, and device change notifications from IPS and IDS devices (security events)
How to put it in place: Configure the devices to send syslog or traps to FortiNAC; config system interface; edit port1; append allowaccess syslog; next; end
Source: FortiNAC-F 7.6.0 Administration Guide, "Open ports" ("FortiNAC Access Configuration": syslog and snmp on port1), "SNMP trap support", and "Security Incidents" ("Implementation": network devices)
